notes.meaning: The psalm opens with a plea for God to be gracious and bless his people, echoing the ancient blessing the priests spoke over Israel in Numbers. Asking for God's face to shine is a request to feel his warm favor and love. The prayer begins with a cry for mercy, because receiving any of God's good gifts always starts with forgiveness of sins.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine explained God's shining face as God revealing what was hidden, or as God rekindling his divine image stamped upon the human soul.

notes.meaning: God's people ask for blessing not for selfish reasons, but so the entire world can see how God works. When surrounding nations see his kindness and rescue, they learn the way of salvation. God blesses his people so they can be a light that draws others to him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine understood both "Your way" and "Your salvation" as direct names for Jesus Christ, who called himself the Way and was recognized by Simeon as God's salvation.

notes.meaning: All groups of people across the globe are invited to thank and praise God. Worship is never meant to stay inside the borders of a single nation. Once people understand God's saving mercy, heartfelt praise naturally follows.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine read the phrase "all the peoples" as a call to belong to the one worldwide Catholic Church rather than regional breakaway groups.

notes.meaning: The nations have every reason to sing with gladness because God rules the world with genuine justice and truth. Unlike human rulers who can be harsh, the Lord leads the peoples gently like a shepherd guiding his flock. Those who know God's salvation look forward to his righteous rule instead of dreading it.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine noted that the nations need not fear God as Judge because he first comes in mercy to correct and straighten their hearts.

notes.meaning: Repeating the chorus word for word underscores the main desire of the whole song. The psalmist earnestly longs to see every nation give its worship to the one true God alone. It shows strong confidence that the day of worldwide praise will surely arrive.

The fields have produced a bountiful harvest, serving as clear proof of God's generous care for his people. This earthly harvest of crops points to an even greater spiritual harvest, when people from many nations turn to the Lord. Physical blessings remind believers of God's faithfulness to provide for body and soul.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that the earth's fruit represents sinners repenting and praising God after hearing the rain of his preached word.

notes.meaning: God showers his people with goodness so that communities in the farthest corners of the earth will stand in holy awe of him. Biblical fear here means deep reverence and honoring worship, not terror. Knowing God's promises gives his followers great courage to share his name with the world.
